# Stage-0 parity — the RULED instrument against the PUBLISHED one

**Posture:** measurement only. No mechanism, no candidate scored, no data purchased (K=0, $0 spend), no session window selected, no frozen ruling revisited, no existing module edited. Generated by `instrument_parity.py`.

Every published Stage-0 figure in [`RESULTS.md`](RESULTS.md) — the integrity battery, the roll exposure, the declared cost of `ROLL-EXCLUDE-2026-07-31` — was measured on **MYM**, and the same 2026-07-31 ruling set eliminated MYM in favour of a two-sided **MCL** construct (`CONFIG-B-MCL-2026-07-31`). Stage 0 was never run on the instrument that is ruled. This page runs the same battery on all four cached panels, through the **unmodified** `dataroot` / `integrity_1m` / `roll_windows` / `stage1_screen` modules.

**Agreement check.** The `MYM` row reproduces the published page exactly — verdict **FAIL**, 18 zero-bar business days, 82 short sessions of which 1 below 25% completeness, 29 rolls, 87 sessions exposed at 4.65%. **No published figure is contradicted by this harness**, so the differences below are properties of the instruments, not of a changed measurement.

The two 2023-only panels PASS and the two seven-year panels FAIL, both on `no_severely_short_sessions`. That tracks panel LENGTH, not instrument quality: the failing member is the documented 2020-06-30 session at 41/390, which lies outside the one calendar year MCL and M2K cover. Read MCL's PASS as *no severe short session inside 2023*, not as a cleaner panel — and see §2 for what the PASS does not certify.

## 2 — Session windows: three columns, and none of them chosen

`integrity_1m` applies `RTH_OPEN_MIN` 09:30 ET, `RTH_CLOSE_MIN` 16:00 ET and the 16:15–16:30 `HALT_SLOT` **unconditionally** — the module has no product-group awareness. Applying that to an Energy contract is a category error, so it is exposed here rather than silently inherited.

**What MCL's integrity PASS does and does not certify.** `rth_median_complete` and the short-session checks measure data completeness INSIDE the 09:30–16:00 window; neither asks whether that window is the right one. For MYM it is a real venue session — the cash-equity session the contract tracks — and completeness there is meaningful, which is why the check bites: MYM FAILs on 2020-06-30. For MCL the same window carries no venue standing. It holds 28.61% of the contract's bars at a full 390/390 median, while the provisional Energy window holds a different 24.61% at 330 bars per trade date. So the PASS certifies that an arbitrarily chosen 390-minute slice of a 23-hour contract is fully populated. That is true, and it is not the question the ruled configuration needs answered.

The two candidate windows are **not nested** — they overlap 09:30–14:30 and each holds minutes the other does not — so a completeness verdict taken under one does not transfer to the other.

**It is labelled provisional because it is unverified:** 09:00–14:30 ET is the NYMEX WTI open-outcry equivalent as commonly quoted, **not** read off a venue source in this session. Do not quote it as a venue fact.

No fourth window is offered and **none of the three is selected**. Which window governs is an operator ruling; choosing one here, after seeing the bar counts, is precisely the selection effect the program's ruling discipline exists to prevent.

## 3 — What `ROLL-EXCLUDE-2026-07-31` declares against what the ruled instrument pays

The ruling declares its own cost as **4.65%** of sessions, measured on MYM.

| symbol   |   sessions |   sessions_excluded |   measured_pct |   declared_pct |   ratio_measured_to_declared |   usable_sessions |   power_floor |   power_floor_vs_MYM |
|:---------|-----------:|--------------------:|---------------:|---------------:|-----------------------------:|------------------:|--------------:|---------------------:|
| MCL      |        257 |                  36 |          14.01 |           4.65 |                         3.01 |               221 |        0.1318 |                 2.84 |
| M2K      |        258 |                  12 |           4.65 |           4.65 |                         1    |               246 |        0.125  |                 2.69 |
| MYM      |       1871 |                  87 |           4.65 |           4.65 |                         1    |              1784 |        0.0464 |                 1    |
| MNQ      |       1872 |                  87 |           4.65 |           4.65 |                         1    |              1785 |        0.0464 |                 1    |

**MCL pays 14.01%, 3.01× the declared figure**, because it rolls **monthly** (12 rolls across 257 sessions) rather than quarterly, and the exposure window is a fixed 2-session lead per roll. Same rule, same window width, three times the sessions removed.

The two costs compound rather than offset: the ruled panel is **one calendar year** (2023-01-02 → 2023-12-29) against MYM's seven, so after exclusion the Clause-N power floor is **0.1318** against **0.0464** — the minimum detectable `d/s` is 2.84× larger on the instrument the ruling selected.

`M2K` pays the declared figure to two decimals (ratio 1.00): the 4.65% transfers inside the Equity Index group and does not transfer out of it.

**No remedy is proposed.** `ROLL-EXCLUDE-2026-07-31` is frozen, and revisiting a frozen ruling — including re-deriving its declared cost from the instrument it governs — is operator work, not a worker's.

Windows are **declared**, not selected: a pre-2023 limb, the cached-2023 limb the current panels hold, and a beyond-2023 limb reaching the equity panels' 2026-07-29 end. Keys are checked at phase `is` / campaign `C1-3LEG-MAP` **and** at every legacy untagged variant, so a chunk pulled before those flags existed still counts as held.

**Findings, not proposals.** History **beyond 2023 is not cached** for either symbol (0 of 31 monthly chunks each) — extending either panel forward would require a pull, so under `$0 / K=0` it cannot be measured in this fleet. History **before 2023 is very nearly cached** (MCL 17/18 chunks, M2K 43/44), which is the more interesting half: the 2023-only panels are not the limit of what this machine already holds, but neither window is complete, so even a backwards extension is not free. **Nothing was pulled. The gap is the finding.**

## 5 — H-A as measured

**Limb 1 — can the existing modules produce the ruled instrument's profile without modification?** Yes. Every figure above came from importing `dataroot`, `integrity_1m`, `roll_windows`, `stage1_screen`, `cost_pins` and `cache_coverage` unchanged; no file in this directory was edited. Stage 0 is not structurally equity-index-only at the code level.

**Limb 2 — does the profile differ materially from the published MYM profile?** Yes, on all three axes measured: roll cadence (monthly vs quarterly, 3.01× the declared exclusion cost), panel length (one year vs seven, a 2.84× worse power floor), and session definition (the battery's 09:30–16:00 window is a venue session for MYM and an arbitrary slice of a 23-hour Energy contract for MCL).

**But the code-level answer to limb 1 is narrower than it looks**, and that is this page's one concern for the orchestrator: the modules RUN, while `integrity_1m`'s session semantics remain equity-index constants applied to an Energy contract. Running is not validity. Which session window governs MCL is unresolved, and it is a ruling, not a measurement.

## What this page does NOT establish

Nothing here scores a mechanism, admits or eliminates an instrument, re-opens a frozen ruling, or prices a pull. It establishes that the ruled instrument's Stage-0 profile is not the published one, and it hands three unresolved items — the governing session window, the declared-cost delta, and the beyond-2023 data gap — to the operator intact.
